name: Glenn Greenwald
role: Journalist and former constitutional and civil-rights lawyer; Guardian columnist, co-founder of The Intercept, reported the Snowden NSA disclosures; Substack writer and host of System Update
summary: Greenwald is a civil-libertarian journalist whose own writing centres on opposing mass surveillance, state and corporate censorship, the national security state and US military intervention. He defends the Bill of Rights as a check on majorities, wants monopolies broken up, supports trans legal rights and animal protection, and describes both parties' establishments as corrupt. On many economic, social and immigration questions he has stated no clear position of his own.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Argues that mass, indiscriminate surveillance is harmful whatever the security aim (TED talk 2014) and in 2026 says the founding premise is that giving up privacy for security is never worth it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Calls the claim that the First Amendment does not protect hate speech false and says the 'hate speech' label is used to justify censorship; in 2026 lists reduced hateful ideas as a benefit that still never justifies relinquishing free speech.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Says liberty-versus-security trade-offs are never worthwhile, and denounced Canada's emergency civil-liberties-denying powers as despotic and the post-1/6 domestic War on Terror as an authoritarian overreaction.

party-controls-media.rationale: Describes government demands that platforms remove political speech as chilling and authoritarian and cites Supreme Court rulings against state coercion of private censors.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemns repression of dissent as a mark of tyranny whether in adversary states or Western ones (protest bans, emergency powers against protesters, jailing for political transgressions).

political-violence-never.rationale: In 2021 reaffirmed his own line that bringing physical force into political protest is lamentable, usually dangerous and unjustifiable except in the rarest circumstances, so he does not hold the absolute 'never' formulation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Said Dick Cheney belongs in a federal prison or the dock at The Hague and that the Obama administration was wrong not to prosecute the torture regime; also criticised blocking foreign investigations of Bush-era torture (press report of remarks plus 2011 interview).

legalize-drugs.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Argues government secrecy is the linchpin of abuse and that the public has a right to know what is done in its name (Snowden, WikiLeaks); he does not speak to a statutory access-to-records right as such.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Argues the Bill of Rights and judicial review are deliberately anti-majoritarian, so laws restricting speech, religion or due process cannot be validly enacted however popular, and describes unchecked majority rule as majoritarian despotism.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Describes the Bill of Rights as limits the majority may not override even at 80 or 90 percent support, and defends the Court's role in enforcing them.

separated-powers.rationale: Argues the Founders feared unchecked executive war power, cites Federalist papers for Congress's checks, and says power cannot be exercised without checks or it will be abused.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Condemns military and intelligence officials who withheld information from or slow-walked the elected president as Deep State subversion, and warns against empowering the military as a bulwark against elected leaders.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes the Washington establishment of both parties as sustaining crony capitalism, endless war and corporatism, and states his view that the Democratic Party is corrupt.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says giant corporations overriding democratic lawmaking make a system resemble an oligarchy, and in 2009 said Wall Street controls government and has laws written for itself; also testified on the political power of tech monopolies.

ban-cartels.rationale: In sworn House antitrust testimony said there is a consensus about the need to break up monopolies wherever they arise, that monopolies threaten political freedom and competition, and listed breaking up Big Tech among his views.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Calls the power of unaccountable billionaires over political discourse unsustainable and an oligarchic threat to democracy; speaks of tech and finance wealth specifically, not wealth concentration in general.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Denounces crony capitalism and laws written to benefit connected firms (Wall Street in 2009, the bipartisan establishment in 2023); no statement framed as a general rule against legal privileges for business.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Says factory farms should be heavily regulated if not dismantled and Big Tech monopolies broken up; these are sector cases, not a general call for tighter corporate regulation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Says he has long been on the far end on trans rights: in favour of full legal rights, of honouring their gender identity and of opposing efforts to exclude them.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: States that factory farms inflict mass torture on animals and should be heavily regulated or dismantled, and calls animal rights a major cause of his.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Defends the right to publish blasphemous and offensive material, and criticises prosecution of Muslims for political speech; he does not discuss blasphemy statutes by name.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Says left-versus-right is an obsolete framework and that the real division is pro-establishment versus anti-establishment; does not say the best of each side should be combined.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Argues US strikes in Iraq and Syria are not self-defense and calls the 2026 Iran war a war of choice since Iran had not attacked and no attack was imminent; no general pacifist formulation found.

non-intervention.rationale: Said that being drawn into heinous alliances is a reason not to manage other countries' internal affairs, and later criticised US interference abroad; no absolute 'for any reason' statement.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Said Cheney belongs in the dock at The Hague or in a federal prison for torture (press report of his interview); no wider statement on international courts and aggression found.

notes: Source base: his Substack archive (2020-2026, read in full text for free posts), the 2014 TED talk, the 2009 Cato Portugal study, and older interviews. His books were not available as text, so the book-era views are covered only through interviews. Several Substack posts are by guests or paywalled and were not used. Views he describes in others (for example Sanders and Trump on trade or immigration, or Lula's welfare programme) were not counted as his own. No stated position was found on abortion, immigration levels, same-sex marriage, tax, trade, climate or encryption.
